title: Chuck and Josh Make It Through Female Puberty
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain female puberty, from the hypothalamus and GnRH/LH/FSH hormone cascade that starts it, through the stages of breast development, pubic hair, growth spurts, and first period (menarche), to vaginal discharge, menstrual cycle and cramps, PMS, acne, emotional changes, self-cutting, childhood sexual play, and cultural puberty rituals around the world. They close with a listener mail praising their Auto Tune episode and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and framing female puberty
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on female puberty, note it is aimed at girls, parents, and families, stress open communication, and recommend the Stuff Mom Never Told You podcast and doctor-reviewed online resources.

segments.title: Hormonal trigger of puberty
segments.summary: The hosts explain that leptin and body fat signal the hypothalamus to release GnRH, which prompts the pituitary to release LH and FSH. They discuss how being overweight may trigger earlier puberty and how stress and family problems may also be linked to earlier onset, with an evolutionary explanation.

segments.title: Normal age range and early puberty trends
segments.summary: The hosts say puberty typically begins between ages eight and eleven, and describe Marcia Herman-Giddens' work in the 1980s and the 2010 study showing earlier breast development in many girls, and the difference between early puberty and precocious puberty.

segments.title: Puberty stages one and two: ovaries, follicles, and breast development
segments.summary: The hosts describe internal development of the reproductive organs, the roughly two million follicles present at birth, and how one follicle matures each cycle. They cover stage two breast development, bra fitting, and how a mother's breast size and grandmothers' size can hint at a daughter's.

segments.title: Stages three to five: growth spurt, body fat, and adult maturity
segments.summary: The hosts cover stage three with pubic hair, bone growth, and vaginal growth, the growth spurt in which hands and feet grow first, sweating and body odor, stage four body fat gain and irregular early periods, and stage five full maturity around ages fourteen to nineteen.

segments.title: Breast development, menarche, and the menstrual cycle
segments.summary: The hosts explain how breasts develop milk ducts and fatty tissue for nursing, mention an article on how breast milk adapts its antibodies, and describe the menstrual cycle lasting twenty to thirty days, with white discharge appearing about six months before the first period.

segments.title: Vaginal discharge types and period basics
segments.summary: The hosts describe normal and concerning vaginal discharge colors and textures, including clear stretchy mucus during ovulation, brown discharge after a period, and signs of infection. They also explain period blood volume and duration, and when to see a doctor about heavy bleeding.

segments.title: Period shaming, cramps, PMS, and acne
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Celebration Day for Girls program in Australia and the stigma around periods, a survey where few women were positive about menstruation, menstrual cramps, PMS and mood changes, and acne caused by sebum and bacteria, along with skin care tips.

segments.title: Emotions, self-image, and risky behavior in teen years
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the emotional feedback loop of puberty, parent-teen conflict, the importance of open communication and good choices, fashion and self-image, and risks such as eating disorders and self-cutting.

segments.title: Childhood sexual play and masturbation
segments.summary: The hosts say young girls, even ages four and five, may simulate sex or masturbate, which is normal. They advise parents not to shame children and suggest redirecting them calmly.

segments.title: Puberty rituals around the world
segments.summary: The hosts describe seclusion and celebration rituals: the Urubu-Kaapor hair cutting tradition in Brazil, a multi-week seclusion in Ghana, the Jewish bat mitzvah, and the Apache Mountain Spirit dance (morning star dance) after a girl's first period.

segments.title: Listener mail on Auto Tune episode
segments.summary: A listener named Noel praises the Auto Tune episode for letting female guests speak, and the hosts respond. The hosts invite feedback by Twitter, Facebook, email, and the website.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close by encouraging listeners to search for more on female puberty and visit HowStuffWorks.com.
